Code duplications are bad
• Duplicated bugs (harder to fix later)
• Longer programs
• Copy & paste errors
Rule of Thumb - write the code once!
• Code reuse: use the same code several times with
different arguments

What is a function in programming ?
• A function is a block of organized, reusable code that
is used to perform a single, well-defined action
• Function’s inputs determines the outputs
• Specific input is called an argument of a function
• Functions provide better modularity for your
application and a high degree of code reusing

inputs

outputs

Function – definition II
A named sequence of statements that performs a
specific task independently of the remaining code

Modularity
Ernie wrote code calculating ab.
To use the code in 8 different calculations, he:
▪ copy & pasted

assigned arguments
Eight times
Bert came up with a more efficient algorithm to

To update Ernie’s code, he went over the eight

Modularity enables code reuse!
“Modularity is the degree to which a
system's components may be separated
and recombined” (Wikipedia)
▪ Top-down design
▪ Improves maintainability
▪ Enforces logical boundaries between
components

Five calls to four different functions!
→Abstraction

Abstraction
Calculate ln

𝑎2 + 𝑏2

ln of sqrt of sum of squares
double result = Math.log(Math.sqrt(Math.pow(a, 2) + Math.pow(b, 2)));
Math.pow(a, 2) → squares a
Math.pow(b, 2) → squares b
Math.sqrt(...) → takes the square root of their sum

Math.log(...) → computes the natural logarithm (ln)

So – why use functions?
• Modularity - Break a task into smaller sub-tasks
(divide and conquer), enables code reuse
• Maintenance - Solve bugs once

• Abstraction – “Hiding” complexity
• Readability – Main code is shorter, implementation
details are hidden within functions

Good coding practices
• Divide & conquer:
• Disassemble into smaller sub-problems.

• Solve each sub-problem independently.
• Documentation
• Meaningful functions’ and variables’ names.

• Arguments & output description for each
function.
• Summarize each step
